Container.Name: skwod
Container.Overview: Skwod is a private group chat with voice and video calls for you and your friends, and this container is the server for it. Everything is end-to-end encrypted: the server stores only scrambled messages it cannot read. Friends reach it by its key, so you need no domain, no port forwarding and no account anywhere.[br][br]After you press Apply: open this container's Logs and copy the one-time admin token. The admin page is only open on the Unraid box itself, for safety, so from your computer run "ssh -L 3477:127.0.0.1:3477 root@YOUR-UNRAID-ADDRESS", then open http://127.0.0.1:3477 (or click WebUI). Type the token, press Start server, and open the invite on your own phone first: the first person in becomes the owner.[br][br]Step-by-step guide for first-timers: https://github.com/FlayrLabs/skwod/blob/main/docs/UNRAID.md
Container.Requires: Unraid 6.12 or newer with Docker enabled. Outbound internet access over UDP (allowed by default on home networks). Nothing needs forwarding on your router.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Where the server keeps everything: the encrypted messages and attachments, and the keys that ARE your server's address. Leave the default. Back this folder up (the appdata backup plugin covers it); if it is lost, your skwod is gone and every invite stops working.

Config.Name: Connection port (UDP)
Config.Description: UDP port your friends' apps (chat AND voice/video calls) use to reach this server. Leave 47474. Port forwarding is NOT needed; forwarding this one UDP port on your router is optional and makes faster, direct connections more likely. If you change this number, put the same number in 'P2P port' (Show more settings).

Config.Name: Admin page address
Config.Description: Leave as is. This is the admin page's address INSIDE the container. On the Unraid box it is published on 127.0.0.1 only (see Extra Parameters: -p 127.0.0.1:3477:3477), so nobody else on your network can open it; you reach it through an SSH tunnel. It also needs the one-time token from the container's log.

Config.Name: Wait for Start button
Config.Description: Leave true. The server serves nobody until you press Start server on the admin page, so nobody can claim it before you. After that it starts by itself on every restart.

Config.Name: P2P port
Config.Description: Leave 47474. Must be the same number as 'Connection port (UDP)'.

Config.Name: Run as (uid:gid)
Config.Description: Leave 99:100 (Unraid's usual nobody:users). The container starts as root only long enough to give the appdata folder to this user, then drops every privilege before it talks to the network.

Config.Name: Use public relays as a fallback
Config.Description: Leave true. When a friend's app cannot connect directly (common behind home routers), traffic goes through a public relay instead. It stays end-to-end encrypted; the relay only sees IP addresses and timing. false = direct connections only: more private, but some friends may not be able to connect at all.

Config.Name: Find on local network
Config.Description: Leave empty (off). Lets phones on your home Wi-Fi find the server faster, but only works with Network Type set to Host. Can also be switched on the admin page.
